# Signatories and community support

Shaurita D. Hutchins and Samuel Bharti are PhD candidates at the University of Alabama at Birmingham and will co-lead the project.

**Hutchins will lead educational design and community development.** She will coordinate the example tutorials and develop the metadata schema. Her experience in open-source training and Carpentries instruction will inform the accessibility guidance and contribution process she develops. Trained in genetics, genomics, and bioinformatics, she combines computational biology with reproducible R/Bioconductor workflows. Her [Prioritizing Candidate Genetic Variants Using GTEx, HuBMAP, and IDG](https://cfdetrainingcenter.github.io/candidate-genetic-variants/) module for the CFDE Training Center includes coding activities that run in the browser and knowledge checks.

**Bharti will lead software architecture and engine integration.** He will connect the package to existing engine checks through adapters that produce common validation reports. His teaching work includes [r-for-beginners](https://github.com/samuelbharti/r-for-beginners), an adaptation of Software Carpentry lessons with slides. He also develops the R packages bioclients, biohttp, and biobouncer, and publishes package documentation through GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.

We will jointly design the package API and registry, and share responsibility for governance and the example tutorials.

We requested public feedback through [r/Stats](https://www.reddit.com/r/Stats/comments/1wvj3wd/for_people_who_teach_or_learn_r_how_do_you_find/) and the [learnr webR discussion](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944771998). Community contributor [\@coatless](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944898742) directed us to learnr2 and Quarto Live, prompting us to focus on shared metadata and checks. This was feedback on related tools; the proposed schema still needs review. We will seek engine maintainers' feedback on the schema and the checks each adapter can support.

We will also consult Carpentries and Bioconductor educators, along with university and community instructors. We will add documented feedback and letters of support as received.
